action_items: Aisha: Share pricing sheet and quickstart repo by Friday 2026-07-17
Ben: Provision sandbox credentials and run sample latency test for VerseCloud by 2026-07-20
Priya: Provide internal compliance checklist and list of required controls by 2026-07-19
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Aisha, Ben, Marco (Redwood); Lydia, Omar, Priya, Tom (VerseCloud)

00:00:03 Aisha: Hey everyone uh thanks for joining we've got about 45 minutes, mainly want to run through the SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, auth setup, and a quick demo of the Console and Optimize suggestions. Also allocate time for Q&A at the end.

00:00:22 Lydia: Sounds good, we're coming from a pretty standard microservices stack, k8s on EKS, and we want to figure out how Redwood would fit for our product recommendations workload. Latency's critical for us, and we have some compliance needs.

00:00:36 Ben: Great, thanks Lydia. Quick question on traffic profile — is this mostly synchronous user-facing calls or batch embedds?

00:00:45 Lydia: Primarily sync for recommendations, about 150 qps peak per region, with some nightly batch embedding jobs.

00:00:53 Omar: And our current pipeline uses OpenAI for prototyping, but we want to reduce cost and get better SLAs. We also have a VPC requirement for the production env.

00:01:05 Priya: Security side — we need SOC 2, SSO integration, audit logs, and KMS/HSM for key management. Also data residency for EMEA customers.

00:01:19 Aisha: Perfect, we'll cover Redwood's Private and Dedicated options briefly and show auth flows in the SDK. Marco will demo the Console Optimize tab for batching and caching suggestions.

00:01:33 Marco: I'll start by sharing my screen — okay see my screen? This is the Redwood Console — top left is the model catalog, here's our standard gpt-like models and Mistral variants, and over here the Optimize tab shows recommendations.

00:01:50 Marco: Take this workload profile example — we detect short prompt + short responses. Optimize suggests enabling prefix KV caching and a batch size of 8 with a latency SLO of 120ms. It also flags that a quantized model variant would reduce GPU memory and cost; note that's a tradeoff for a slight quality delta.

00:02:20 Tom: How are those recommendations generated? Is it based on our traces or a generic heuristic?

00:02:28 Marco: Both — we ingest route-level traces, token distributions, and you can upload a representative trace file. The recommendations are workload-aware but we always encourage running a pilot or a bench.

00:02:41 Ben: Okay switching to the SDK quickstart — I'll show the Python flow first.

00:02:48 05:00 Ben: (screen) Here's a minimal Python example, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or use an ephemeral token via SSO, then: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client=RedwoodClient(); resp = client.responses.create(prompt="Recommend 3 products for user X", max_tokens=64) — response streaming works out of the box, and we show how to use the async SDK for high concurrency.

00:03:23 Omar: Do we have a TypeScript snippet? Our node services are TS.

00:03:28 Ben: Yep — example: import {Redwood} from '@redwood-inference/sdk'; const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}); const r = await client.responses.create({input: '...'}) — shows both promise and streaming with event listeners.

00:03:45 Lydia: Auth — can you show the SSO service account flow? We need to rotate keys and use short lived tokens.

00:03:54 Ben: Absolutely. For enterprise we recommend using SAML SSO to Redwood Console. You map groups to roles and create service principals which can mint short-lived API keys. You can also integrate KMS for envelope encryption; our docs show a sample with AWS KMS.

00:04:12 Priya: Any HSM integration? We use 3rd party HSM for root keys.

00:04:18 Marco: We support customer-managed keys via KMS and there's an HSM option for the Private deployment; we'll share the architecture doc.

00:04:29 10:00 Ben: Back to the SDK — one gotcha: ensure you pin the SDK version and the model version in your code to avoid silent regressions. We show a sample config file and an env var pattern: REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-v1-small.

00:04:45 Omar: How do we run local dev vs production? Do you support a local mock server?

00:04:51 Ben: We provide a lightweight CLI devserver that can emulate basic responses for local tests, but for performance testing you should hit the sandbox hosted endpoint. We'll give you sandbox creds.

00:05:06 Lydia: What about rate limits and retries?

00:05:11 Ben: SDK includes an exponential backoff retry policy with jitter. Rate limits are enforced per-account and per-route; the SDK exposes headers for remaining quota.

00:05:28 Marco: Now I'll demo an end-to-end quickstart: create an API key, call the Python example, then enable prefix caching via the Console route settings — I'll change the route to use dedicated model variant, toggle caching, and show estimated cost impact.

00:05:50 Marco: (click) You can see cost estimate updated in real time; this route is currently using hosted capacity but you can switch to Dedicated if you have committed capacity.

00:06:08 Priya: The audit logs — do they include request bodies or are they metadata-only? For compliance we need redaction options.

00:06:16 Aisha: Good question — by default audit logs have metadata and request IDs; payloads can be optionally logged or redacted based on route policies. For Private we support per-customer retention and egress controls.

00:06:32 Tom: Data residency — can we restrict model hosting to eu-west for EU tenants?

00:06:40 Marco: Yes — region pinning in the Console and routing policies let you force EU-only inference. Dedicated or Private gives stronger guarantees.

00:06:52 15:00 Ben: Quick dev ops note: for high throughput we recommend the async client with streaming, use connection pooling, and configure consistent batch sizes. There's a snippet for aiohttp connector reuse in the quickstart.

00:07:08 Omar: Do you provide SDK telemetry for traces so we can correlate traces in Jaeger/Datadog?

00:07:15 Ben: SDK emits trace headers and we can inject OpenTelemetry spans. The Console can ingest traces to show latency breakdown per token and per model.

00:07:29 Lydia: Let's talk cost — do you have a cost estimator for 150 qps and 2-token prompt average?

00:07:36 Marco: Yes there's a workbook; we'll run a quick estimate offline but Optimize gives ballpark unit costs and suggests quantization or batching to cut cost by 30-60% depending on quality tolerance.

00:07:50 Priya: Security docs — can you share SOC 2 report and your penetration test summary?

00:07:56 Aisha: We'll send SOC 2 Type II and the pen test exec summary. For Private deployments we can sign an MSA and support extra security controls.

00:08:08 Ben: Back to the code, demoing streaming: the TS SDK example subscribes to onChunk callbacks. For Python async iter you do 'async for chunk in resp.stream()' — we also show how to do partial reranking with embeddings in the same flow.

00:08:32 Omar: Embeddings — how are they billed and stored? We want ephemeral storage and retention policies.

00:08:39 Marco: Embeddings are per-unit billed. You can opt out of storage at route-level; otherwise we store for a configurable retention and expose deletion APIs. Private gives you full control.

00:08:57 22:00 Lydia: I'm concerned about cold-start latency on Dedicated.

00:09:03 Marco: Dedicated pools keep GPUs warm; you can configure minimum replica counts and autoscale based on queue depth. For very low-latency SLOs we recommend pinned instances.

00:09:16 Ben: Another integration tip: instrument request ids from your gateway and forward them to Redwood for traceability.

00:09:24 Priya: For compliance we'll need SSO provisioning and RBAC for the Console. How granular is role mapping?

00:09:31 Aisha: Roles map to Console and API permissions; you can create custom roles and map SAML groups. We'll share the role matrix.

00:09:44 Tom: Any managed migrations from OpenAI? We want a runbook.

00:09:49 Marco: We have migration docs and a benchmarking playbook. SE team can run a baseline and suggest model variants to match quality.

00:10:02 30:00 Ben: Let's go through a short live SDK test — I'll paste a small script into the chat. (Ben pastes) Run it locally with REDWOOD_API_KEY set to sandbox key.

00:10:28 Omar: Running it now... getting a 200 and streaming chunks. Latency ~95ms from my laptop to sandbox in us-east.

00:10:40 Ben: Nice, that matches expected. We'll capture those traces for Optimize.

00:10:48 Lydia: Ok recap and next steps?

00:10:52 Aisha: Recap: we'll send quickstart repo, pricing and security docs; Ben will provision sandbox creds and run a sample bench; Marco will share Optimize workbook and model recommendations; Priya will send compliance questions to Aisha. We'll aim to schedule a POC scoping call next week.

00:11:12 Priya: One more — can we get a detailed dataflow diagram for Private deployment?

00:11:18 Marco: Yes we'll attach the Private deployment diagram.

00:11:24 Lydia: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.

00:11:30 Aisha: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.

End of call.
